question.problem: Find the numbers $c$ such that the average value of $f(x)=3{x}^{2}-6x-10$ on the interval $[0,c]$ is equal to $8.$
question.worked_solution:
To solve for $c,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ 8 & =\frac{1}{c-0}{\int }_{0}^{c}(3{x}^{2}-6x-10)\,\text{d}x \\ 8 & ={\frac{1}{c}({x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}-10x)|}_{0}^{c} \\ 8 & =\frac{1}{c}[({c}^{3}-3{c}^{2}-10c)-0] \\ 8 & ={c}^{2}-3c-10 \\ 0 & ={c}^{2}-3c-18 \\ 0 & =(c+3)(c-6) \\ c & =-3,\,6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $c>0,$ we conclude that $c=6$ only.
